newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary police chiefs sacked over gang war.
newsitem.headline: Hungary police chiefs sacked over gang war.

text.p: The Hungarian government sacked the chiefs of the national and Budapest police on Friday for failing to halt gangland bombings and shootings in the capital.
Since September, Budapest resident have been rattled by 11 bombings and five shootings -- apparently in a war of organised gangs. One man has been killed and two have been badly injured.
The latest shooting was on Friday morning when an attacker shot at a 52-year-old Budapest casino owner and struck him with his gun before fleeing.
A government statement said that Prime Minister Gyula Horn and Interior Minister Gabor Kuncze decided to sack national police chief Sandor Pinter and Budapest police chief Janos Bodracska.
"Personnel changes are needed to improve public safety and the fight the spread of crime," the statement said.
Bodracska had told reporters earlier in the day that two men detained overnight were caught with 28 hand grenades and other explosives and were suspected of supplying gang bombers.
A hand grenade can be bought on the Budapest black market for 10,000 forints ($60), the police chief said.
According to Bodracska, the gangland war began over money borrowed by an underworld figure at high interest,
"He used the money and the sum was dwindling, and when it got too low, he disappered," Bodracska said. "Now we cannot find him and (the gangs) can't either."
